chunks: And from it, in his address to his companions:

You have reached a station of Allah's honour for you such that your slave-girls are honoured by it, your neighbours are connected to you by it, and those who have no superiority over you honour you, and those who have no power over you fear you. You see the covenants of Allah being broken yet you do not get angry! While you are indignant at the breaking of the pledges of your fathers! The affairs of Allah used to come to you, originate from you, and return to you; so you gave the oppressors authority over your position, threw your reins into their hands, and surrendered Allah's affairs to them. They act in doubts and walk in desires. By Allah, if they scattered you under every star, Allah would surely gather you for the evil of their day!
ai.seo_question: What is the critique of the companions' loss of authority in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: This passage from Nahj al-Balagha serves as a profound critique of the political passivity of the early Muslim community, illustrating how the surrender of authority to unjust rulers led to the erosion of divine covenants. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the correlation between social justice and spiritual integrity, warning that collective negligence in governance invites divine retribution even if the community is scattered. The Imam contrasts their sensitivity to human political betrayals with their indifference to the violation of God's rights, highlighting a critical shift in communal responsibility.

en.sayed-ali-raza: [A part of the same sermon addressed to his followers :]

By bounty of Allāh over you, you have acquired a position where even your slave maids are honoured, your neighbours are treated well. Even he over whom you enjoy no distinction or obligation honours you. Even those people fear you who had no apprehension of attack from you or any authority over you. You now see pledges of Allāh being broken but do not feel enraged although you fret and frown on the breaking of traditions of your forefathers. Allāh’s matters have been coming to you, and going from and again coming back to you; but you have made over your place to wrong-doors and thrown towards them your responsibilities, and have placed Allāh’s affairs in their hands. They act in doubts and tread in (fulfilment of) desires. By Allāh, even if they disperse you under every star Allāh would surely collect you on the day that would be worst for them.
